what: highlight "concluding an 89.2% loss for the index in less than three years"
said: By July nineteen thirty-two, the Dow had lost eighty-nine percent of its value.

what: highlight "The Dow Jones did not return to its peak close of September 3, 1929, for 25 years"
said: So the Millers' stock jar went from one thousand dollars to about one hundred ten dollars. And it took twenty-five years to get back.

what: highlight "all experienced drops in personal income , prices ( deflation )"
said: What about cash? Here is the surprise. During the Great Depression, prices fell. That is called deflation, the opposite of inflation.

what: highlight "9,000 of its 25,000 banks had gone out of business"
said: But there is a big catch. Cash in a bank was not safe. By nineteen thirty-three, nine thousand of America's twenty-five thousand banks had gone out of business.

what: highlight "By 1933, the U.S. unemployment rate had risen to 25%"
said: And unemployment had reached twenty-five percent. One in four workers had no job, so even people with savings were spending them just to eat.

what: highlight "the hoarding of gold coin"
said: On April fifth, nineteen thirty-three, President Roosevelt signed an order banning Americans from hoarding gold coins and gold bars.

what: highlight "were arrested with $15,000 in gold"
said: People had to turn in their gold at the old price. Some who refused were actually arrested.

what: highlight "Dollar from $20.67 to $35 an ounce."
said: Then the government changed the official gold price from twenty dollars sixty-seven to thirty-five dollars an ounce. A jump of almost seventy percent.

what: highlight "December 31, 1974"
said: That ban lasted a very long time. It was not repealed until the end of nineteen seventy-four. For over forty years, regular Americans could not legally hold gold bars.

what: highlight "about one-third of farmers had lost their land"
said: Bonds from the US government kept paying, and in a world of falling prices, those fixed payments were worth more. The house jar? Farm and home prices fell hard, and about a third of farmers lost their land.

what: highlight "crop prices fell by up to 60%"
said: Crop prices fell by up to sixty percent. A farm that looked like a safe asset in nineteen twenty-nine could not even pay its own loan by nineteen thirty-two.

what: highlight "We now have the worst of both worlds"
said: Economists call this stagflation. Stagnation plus inflation. A British politician described it as the worst of both worlds.

what: highlight "led to rising prices and slowing growth"
said: The oil crisis of nineteen seventy-three was a big part of it. Oil prices jumped, and so did almost everything else.

what: highlight "Stagflation presents a policy dilemma"
said: It also trapped the government. Fighting inflation with higher rates could raise unemployment. Fighting unemployment could make inflation worse.

what: highlight "when the US unilaterally suspended the direct convertibility of the United States dollar to gold"
said: And gold? This was gold's big decade. In nineteen seventy-one, America stopped trading dollars for gold at thirty-five dollars. After that, gold was free to rise.

what: highlight "The Dow Industrials bottomed out a ratio of 1:1 with gold during 1980"
said: By nineteen eighty, gold had shot up so far that one ounce of gold could buy the entire Dow Jones index. One to one.

what: highlight "The notable peak in 1980 followed the Soviet military involvement in Afghanistan"
said: That peak came right after a decade of inflation and oil shocks, and just after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan. Fear was at its highest.

what: highlight "two major frauds were International Gold Bullion Exchange and Bullion Reserve of North America"
said: High gold prices also brought out scammers. In the early nineteen eighties, two big gold investment frauds took people's money.

what: highlight "proceeded to post gains throughout the 1980s and 1990s"
said: That was the peak. Gold had risen after a decade of inflation and oil shocks. And then, after nineteen eighty, stocks went on a long winning run through the nineteen eighties and nineties.

what: highlight "rose by 600%"
said: In the late nineteen nineties, everyone wanted internet stocks. The tech-heavy Nasdaq index rose six hundred percent in five years.

what: highlight "only to fall 78% from its peak by October 2002"
said: Then it peaked in March two thousand and fell seventy-eight percent by October two thousand two.

what: highlight "investors shifted from strong performing technology stocks to poor performing established stocks"
said: If the Millers' stock jar was full of hot tech stocks, it was nearly wiped out. But boring, established companies did much better.

what: highlight "investors seek to sell assets perceived as risky and instead purchase safe assets"
said: That rush has a name. Flight to quality.

what: highlight "Treasury bond is less risky and more liquid than a corporate bond"
said: And the safest, most liquid thing in the world is usually a US Treasury bond.

what: highlight "Housing prices, which peaked in early 2006, started to decline in 2006 and 2007, and reached new lows in 2011."
said: Then they did. Housing prices peaked in early two thousand six and started to fall. They did not hit bottom until twenty eleven.

what: highlight "the Case–Shiller home price index reported the largest price drop in its history"
said: On December thirtieth, two thousand eight, the main index of home prices reported the largest drop in its history.

what: highlight "sales were down 13% to 482,000 from the peak of 554,000 in March 2006"
said: It started slowly. By March two thousand seven, home sales were already down thirteen percent from their peak, and the typical price had slipped.

what: highlight "household wealth in the United States fell $11 trillion"
said: Stocks fell hard too. American household wealth dropped by eleven trillion dollars, from sixty-one trillion to about fifty trillion.

what: highlight "European banks lost more than $1 trillion on toxic assets"
said: Banks were hit too. American and European banks lost more than a trillion dollars on bad loans and toxic assets.

what: highlight "An example is subprime mortgage crisis in 2008."
said: And yet, the bond jar did it again. During the subprime crisis of two thousand eight, money fled into Treasury bonds.

what: highlight "It was the fastest correction in market history from all-time high"
said: In February twenty twenty, the pandemic hit. Stocks fell so fast it set a record. It took just six days to drop ten percent from the top.

what: highlight "Treasury securities fell to 0.82% and 1.34% respectively"
said: Even safe bond yields fell to record lows, because so much money rushed into them at once.

what: highlight "offered at least $1.5 trillion worth of short-term loans to banks"
said: In one move, the New York Federal Reserve offered at least one and a half trillion dollars in short-term loans to banks.

what: highlight "U.S. market indices did not return to January 2020 levels until November 2020"
said: By April, stocks around the world had started rising again. American indices were back to their January levels by November.

what: highlight "gold prices increased above $4,000 per troy ounce for the first time"
said: In October twenty twenty-five, gold rose above four thousand dollars an ounce for the first time, after climbing more than fifty percent in one year.
